request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My API has a property literally named a.b and another indexed field at key 0. Can I use "a.b" and are empty arrays valid keys?
required_points: Use ["a.b"] for the literal segment; "a.b" splits.
Zero is a key; empty array/string and null/undefined are keyless.
Do not assume quoted bracket expressions are parsed.
forbidden_claims: Zero is keyless.
String and array paths always mean the same thing.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Two visible widgets use customer.email and seem to share validity. Does setting shareFormControl false guarantee independent submitted values?
required_points: Same-path lookup can reuse one control; supplied formControl wins before the sharing flag.
The flag skips lookup but does not create distinct model paths or promise independent parent registrations.
forbidden_claims: Duplicate keys guarantee independent model values.
shareFormControl false overrides a supplied field.formControl.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: A second visible field with the same key adds a validator and my first widget becomes invalid. Is that possible, and are hidden participants included?
required_points: Multiple registered fields contribute composed validators.
The shared-field merge filters hidden participants.
Keyless child groups can also contribute.
forbidden_claims: Only the edited widget contributes validators.
All hidden participants are always included.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I add a rule with control.setValidators and later replace the fields input. Is the rule guaranteed to survive, or should it be represented in Formly configuration?
required_points: The fields-change path recursively clears validators and field registrations.
Rebuild installs Formly configuration; ad-hoc additions are not guaranteed to survive.
forbidden_claims: Manual validators always survive every rebuild.
Applications should routinely invoke internal registration helpers.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: A registered type supplies a label and a flag. Why can my label: "" or null be replaced while false and 0 survive? Is that also defaultValue behavior?
required_points: Reverse merging fills null/undefined/empty string and preserves false/zero.
Model defaultValue is a different undefined-only fallback.
forbidden_claims: Null and empty string always block type defaults.
Model defaultValue overwrites null because reverse merge does.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My type defaultOptions supplies wrappers and parsers arrays. Will a field array concatenate with those defaults, and does [] behave like a missing value?
required_points: Existing arrays are not recursively merged or concatenated by reverseDeepMerge.
An empty array survives; null/undefined/empty string take the fill branch.
forbidden_claims: Arrays always concatenate.
An empty array is treated as missing.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Can I clone a built field containing a FormControl, a Map of mutable objects and an Observable, then serialize it as an independent reusable config?
required_points: AbstractControl becomes null; Map/Set entries are shallow; Observable/functions may retain identity.
Do not promise universal deep copy or JSON persistence of built runtime config.
forbidden_claims: Map entries are recursively cloned.
FormControl is copied as an independent working control.
Every typed array is supported.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: If I enable extras.immutable, can I treat every nested object and the built controls as frozen and detached from my input?
required_points: The host clones incoming data using Formly clone.
No freezing; specialized cloning has identity/shallow-copy limits.
forbidden_claims: immutable freezes controls and every nested object.
It guarantees universal deep detachment.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Can props.attributes: { compareWith: "myFn", customValidator: "check" } wire Angular inputs and validation on my custom widget?
required_points: It sets DOM attributes, not Angular function inputs or validators.
Use renderer bindings/configuration and control integration for those behaviors.
forbidden_claims: Attribute strings automatically become Angular input functions.
The attributes directive implements a custom value accessor.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I start a subscription in hooks.onInit and expect hiding then showing the field to stop and restart it. Does lazy rendering guarantee that, and does onChanges run on every model edit?
required_points: Outer hooks and inner rendered component lifetime differ.
Lazy hiding clears inner container without necessarily destroying the outer field.
onChanges is about the field input, not every model edit.
forbidden_claims: Every hide triggers hooks.onDestroy.
Every show reruns hooks.onInit.
Every model edit triggers hooks.onChanges.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Our server sends field.template containing <my-widget [value]="model.x">. Will safeHtml activate that Angular binding, or should we use an inline type?
required_points: innerHtml does not compile Angular bindings.
safeHtml bypasses HTML trust handling, not a compiler.
Use registered type or declared formlyTemplate matched by field.type.
forbidden_claims: safeHtml safely compiles arbitrary server Angular templates.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Can I accept arbitrary customer-authored expression strings because Formly evaluates them in a sandbox, including under a CSP that forbids dynamic code?
required_points: Function constructor executes expressions; no sandbox.
Do not promise operation under restrictive dynamic-code CSP.
forbidden_claims: Formly string expressions are sandboxed.
All restrictive CSPs are supported.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: A blog imports provideFormlyConfig from @ngx-formly/core and calls ɵreverseDeepMerge as its extension API. Are those supported v6.3.12 setup contracts?
required_points: provideFormlyConfig is absent from the pinned public barrel.
Use established FormlyModule configuration; ɵ exports are not evidence of a stable application extension API.
forbidden_claims: provideFormlyConfig is a v6.3.12 package export.
Every exported ɵ helper is a stable public application API.

request: My application uses Formly 7 with Material. Can you guarantee that these merge, clone and hook lifetime contracts apply unchanged?
required_points: The available exact-6.3.12 knowledge does not establish release-7 behavior.
State the version coverage gap rather than asserting compatibility.
forbidden_claims: These behaviors are verified for Formly 7.

request: I use Formly 6.3.12 with Bootstrap. Please certify the complete Bootstrap widget interaction and browser rendering behavior from your Material/core sources.
required_points: Core implementation evidence does not certify Bootstrap renderer/browser interaction.
State the adapter qualification gap.
forbidden_claims: Material/core source certifies complete Bootstrap browser behavior.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My key is "customer['email']". Does the key parser evaluate it as a JavaScript member expression?
required_points: The key parser only normalizes bracket word-character segments, then splits dots.
Quoted bracket expressions are not a general supported JavaScript parser; use explicit path segments.
forbidden_claims: It evaluates JavaScript property expressions.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: With extras.immutable, I mutate an object stored as a Map value in the incoming model. Does the clone guarantee a separate nested object?
required_points: Map entries are shallow copied by Formly clone.
immutable does not guarantee deep separation of that entry object.
forbidden_claims: All Map entry values are deep cloned.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My field sets wrappers: [] while the type has defaultOptions.wrappers. Will reverseDeepMerge refill the empty array?
required_points: Empty arrays survive reverseDeepMerge.
Arrays are not recursively merged or concatenated in this utility.
forbidden_claims: The default wrappers automatically replace an empty array.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: Can I turn on props.safeHtml to make untrusted field.template HTML safe before inserting it?
required_points: safeHtml invokes bypassSecurityTrustHtml.
That is a trust bypass, not sanitization or Angular template compilation.
forbidden_claims: safeHtml sanitizes untrusted HTML to make it safe.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I replace props.attributes with a new object omitting my old data-tracking key. Does formlyAttributes retain the old keys or remove them?
required_points: The replacement observer removes previous keys then sets current non-null entries.
These are DOM attributes rather than automatic Angular inputs.
forbidden_claims: All omitted old attributes are retained.
